• No internet required to play
• Higher audio quality possible (e.g. uncompressed WAV on CD vs compressed MP3 streaming)
• Cannot be lost to server outages or licensing changes
Conclusion should weigh target audience preferences, costs, and the artist’s goals.

expect:
Top band (7-8): Thorough discussion covering both formats with a reasoned conclusion. QWC: specialist terminology used accurately.
Mid band (4-6): Sound discussion of both formats.
Lower band (1-3): Basic comparison.
Indicative content:
JPEG advantages:
• Smaller file sizes due to lossy compression, meaning faster page loading
• Widely supported across all browsers and devices
• Best for photographs and images with many colours
JPEG disadvantages:
• Does not support transparency
• Quality degrades each time the file is re-saved
PNG advantages:
• Supports transparency (alpha channel) — essential for logos on varied backgrounds
• Lossless compression preserves full quality
• Can be re-saved without quality loss
PNG disadvantages:
• Larger file sizes than JPEG
• Not as efficient for photographs with millions of colours
Conclusion: depends on use — JPEG for photos, PNG for logos and graphics needing transparency.

expect:
Top band (7-8): Thorough discussion of both formats with clear analysis and a reasoned conclusion. QWC: specialist terminology used accurately.
Mid band (4-6): Sound discussion covering both sides.
Lower band (1-3): Basic comparison.
Indicative content:
MP3:
• Very small file sizes due to lossy compression (typically 3–4 MB per song)
• Universally supported on all devices and platforms
• Faster to download and stream, using less bandwidth
• However, some audio quality is permanently lost
FLAC:
• Preserves 100% of the original audio quality using lossless compression
• Preferred by audiophiles who value high-fidelity sound
• Open-source with no licensing fees
• However, file sizes are much larger (10–30 MB per song)
• Requires more bandwidth to stream and more storage to host
• Not supported on all devices, particularly some older hardware
Conclusion: MP3 is better for mass distribution where accessibility matters; FLAC is better for high-quality niche audiences willing to accept larger downloads.

expect:
Top band (7-8): Thorough discussion of both sides with clear analysis and a reasoned conclusion. QWC: specialist terminology used accurately.
Mid band (4-6): Sound discussion covering both sides.
Lower band (1-3): Basic comparison.
Indicative content:
4K advantages:
• 3840 × 2160 pixels — four times the detail of 1080p
• Much sharper, more detailed image, especially on large screens
• Better for cinema and high-end home viewing
• Increasingly standard on premium streaming platforms
4K disadvantages:
• File sizes are significantly larger, requiring more storage and faster internet for streaming
• Requires powerful hardware to edit and render
• Not all viewers have 4K-capable displays — the extra quality is wasted on HD screens
• Higher bandwidth costs for streaming providers
1080p advantages:
• Smaller file sizes, easier to stream and store
• Universally supported on all modern devices
• Still provides excellent quality for most viewing situations
Conclusion: 4K is best for premium content where quality is paramount; 1080p remains the practical standard for mass distribution.
